observation_summary: The compiler crashes with a NullPointerException when processing an interface that extends multiple non-existent types.
reasoning_summary: The crash occurs in TypeCheck.java at line 1574, where the code attempts to call getOwnPropertyNames() on an object returned by interfaceType.getImplicitPrototype(). The code assumes that the implicit prototype of an interface is always a valid object. However, when an interface extends a non-existent type, the type system may return null for the implicit prototype, leading to a NullPointerException when the code attempts to dereference it.
